metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Windows: single-instance window reuse + Explorer multi-select as one playlist
tasks.description: Make Windows match the macOS open idiom (LaunchServices already gives the Mac one instance + one openURLs batch). Today each Explorer double-click/Open spawns a FULL new process (decode pool + resident VRAM ring each; settings.toml write races), and multi-select Open invokes one process per file (Explorer blocks >15 selections by default — MultipleInvokePromptMinimum — so the blast radius is capped at ~15 processes, but that is still bad). Plan: (a) accept multiple CLI path args -> classify_inputs (the Vec<PathBuf> -> LaunchInput::Files machinery already serves drag-drop/picker); (b) MultiSelectModel=Player on the ProgID (MSI AppRegistration component + the HKCU self-registration fallback in default_app.rs) so a multi-select arrives as ONE invocation; (c) single-instance: named mutex, loser forwards its paths via WM_COPYDATA to the running instance (-> open_paths -> open_plan) and exits, winner comes to front (AllowSetForegroundWindow) — this also merges the multiple invocations Explorer emits when a huge selection overflows the ~32K command line. Compare-two-photos is NOT this task: thats #43 (or a future explicit File > New Window command, which the mutex design must not preclude — e.g. a --new-window flag bypass). MSIX/Store evaluation moved out to decisions.md (revisit only if monetizing). Windows machine required.
tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.

tasks.title: AI image description (on-device / local models only)
tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (2026-07-03; HUD/panel target revised 2026-07-05 by task #54). Describe the current image with a vision model. Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Auto mode is an opt-in toggle: fine by construction on the Apple on-device backend, but a configured endpoint could be remote, and passive sends must be a deliberate choice. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. Custom prompt template = advanced, settings.toml-only in v1 ({filename}/{folder}/{datetime}/{location}/{camera} placeholders). Optional TTS via CoreEffect::Speak — AVSpeechSynthesizer / Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis, offline system voices, speech stops on navigation. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Privacy (ADR-018): never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk; the endpoint URL + toggles are the only persisted config. v1 scope: on-disk stills (archive entries punted like Delete). Interim HUD note: pb-hud font fallback helps the current paragraph renderer and non-Latin EXIF/text values, but task #54 makes Description/Ask a rich panel with selectable/copyable text; the HUD is not the final rich-text surface. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images). || WWDC26 CONFIRMED (2026-07-04, https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/): FM image input is NEW in the 2026 release (macOS 27) — on-device, ships with the OS, no download/setup; API is session.respond { PROMPT; Attachment(x) } where x = NSImage/CGImage/CIImage/CVPixelBuffer/file-URL, any size/aspect. VQA confirmed — the model answers ARBITRARY user questions about an image, not just captions (new subtask 9). WARNING: the 2M-first-time-downloads cap the owner saw is on PRIVATE CLOUD COMPUTE (the cloud escalation tier), NOT the free on-device model; and PCC is CLOUD, so per ADR-018 (never cloud by our hand) we request the ON-DEVICE model ONLY and never PCC — the cap does not constrain us. 3rd-party server models (Anthropic/Google) also plug into the FM framework, billed per-token — not our path. Subtask 2 (prompt builder) DONE 2026-07-04. || COPY + ASK DONE 2026-07-04: Copy AI description (Edit + context menus, both shells) + Ask about image (Shift+D, multi-line dialog, both shells) landed — see subtask 9.

tasks.title: Evaluate Velopack: modern install UX + auto-updates for the Windows channel
tasks.description: Owner call (2026-07-03): 'auto updates are kinda non-optional in 2026.' Velopack (the maintained Squirrel successor, first-class Rust crate `velopack`) gives the Chrome/Discord install model — double-click, no wizard, installed + launched in seconds, per-user in %LocalAppData%, with built-in DELTA AUTO-UPDATES from a simple static feed (GitHub Releases works as the feed). This is an EVALUATION task, not a committed cutover: decide whether Velopack becomes the primary consumer channel (MSI kept for perMachine/enterprise), the beta channel only, or isn't a fit. Distinct from MSIX (still parked, ADR-018): Velopack is unpackaged Win32, so the registry integrations stay ordinary registry writes.
tasks.details: Questions the spike must answer: (1) Integration cost — the velopack crate wants a VelopackApp::build().run() hook at process start (fast-exit update hooks) in pb-app's main; measure its startup cost against the keypress→photon budget (should be ~0 when no update event, but MEASURE, per the prime directive). (2) File associations + the folder verb: Velopack installs per-user with a stable %LocalAppData% path — port the MSI's HKCR writes to HKCU\Software\Classes self-registration at install/update hook time (PhotoBlaze already has HKCU self-registration code from the 'Set default…' work, task #14.1) and confirm Open-with + Default-apps behave identically to the MSI install. (3) Update UX: silent background download + apply-on-restart (the viewer restarts in ms, so this fits) vs a toast offering restart-now; where the check runs (startup + daily?), and it must respect privacy #2 — an update CHECK is a network call, so it needs an off switch in Settings and must never phone home viewing data (it doesn't, but say so in the privacy notes). (4) Signing: vpk pack signs with signtool args — confirm Azure Trusted Signing /dlib flags pass through cleanly (same dlib/dmdf as release-windows.ps1). (5) Channel strategy: GitHub Releases as the update feed (vpk upload github), MSI + Velopack artifacts side by side on the same release; decide whether the MSI stays the website default. (6) Uninstall/upgrade coexistence: installing the Velopack build alongside an existing MSI install — define the migration story (likely: Velopack setup detects the MSI product and offers to remove it, or docs just say uninstall first). Output: a decisions.md ADR with the verdict + a working spike branch producing a signed Velopack setup.exe + one exercised delta update.
tasks.testStrategy: Spike acceptance: a signed PhotoBlaze Velopack setup.exe installs per-user with working file associations; publishing a second version to a test GitHub release delivers a delta update that applies on restart; startup overhead of the Velopack hook measured and recorded (target: unmeasurable against the 8.3 ms frame budget); the update check has a Settings off switch; ADR written with the channel decision.

tasks.title: Vendor-patch wgpu-hal: presentsWithTransaction during window-mode transitions (flash-free resize, MTKView-grade)
tasks.description: Make the fullscreen-toggle / resize composite pixel-perfect on macOS. Today's mitigation (2026-07-04) is benign-not-atomic: layerContentsPlacement=.center + contentsGravity on the canvas view means the one racy composite ({new bounds, previous drawable} — wgpu presents out-of-band from the CA transaction that moves the bounds) shows UNSCALED stale content for <=1 frame instead of a stretch. The atomic fix is Apple's presentsWithTransaction (what MTKView flips on during live resize). wgpu-hal 22's Metal backend ALREADY implements the correct present branch (Surface.present_with_transaction pub field; present does commit -> wait_until_scheduled -> drawable.present(); the field's own doc comment cites resize-sensitive UI apps) — but wgpu 22 gives no safe way to SET it: Surface::as_hal hands out only a shared ref, there's no creation-time knob, and configure() re-asserts the flag onto the layer every resize (so flipping the CAMetalLayer property from Swift is useless). PLAN: (1) vendor wgpu-hal 22.0 with a ~20-line patch — interior-mutable flag (AtomicBool) + set_present_with_transaction(&self) — wired via [patch.crates-io] like the sevenz-rust2 precedent; (2) pb-render seam Renderer::set_present_with_transaction(bool) reaching the hal surface through Surface::as_hal; (3) flip it ON only around window-mode transitions (and optionally during live resize), OFF otherwise — presentsWithTransaction costs a main-thread waitUntilScheduled block per present, which MTKView itself only tolerates while resizing; the photo hot path (hold-to-fly) never resizes, keypress->photon untouched; (4) owner drives the upstream PR against wgpu trunk — NOTE trunk's Metal backend was rewritten on objc2 in 23+, so the trunk patch is the same concept but different code; a hal-level setter is the least-bikesheddable API shape. When the eventual egui/wgpu upgrade train moves off 22, the vendored patch drops (if merged) or re-rolls. Payoff is polish: the remaining <=1-frame unscaled reveal on F-toggles/live-resize becomes zero-artifact.

tasks.title: macOS window toolbar — nav + view/panel affordances (NSToolbar)
tasks.description: Owner idea (2026-07-05): a togglable toolbar for mouse-driven control — next/previous/random navigation buttons, toggles for the Inspector and folder-tree panels, and other frequently-used actions (rotate? delete? open?). Tension to resolve with the owner before implementation: CLAUDE.md's prime directive is a borderless, chrome-less window — an always-visible toolbar would contradict that, so 'togglable' likely means hidden by default and revealed on demand (a hotkey, and/or reveal-on-mouse-move-to-edge like fullscreen video players), never persistent chrome that eats into the fit-to-screen image area.
tasks.details:
CRASH FIXED (2026-07-06): setting window.toolbar synchronously inside viewDidMoveToWindow (← attachCanvas ← SwiftUI addSubview realizing the WindowGroup window) crashed in -[NSToolbar _loadAllPlaceholderItems] (SIGTRAP) — re-entrant toolbar mutation mid-realization. Fix: defer the window.toolbar assignment one runloop hop (installToolbarIfNeeded → DispatchQueue.main.async), gated so the per-drain reassertIfClobbered waits for toolbarInstalled=true. autosavesConfiguration stays TRUE (verified NOT the cause; Hide/Customize persist natively). Shipped .app verified launch- and photo-load-clean.

v1.0 landed (2026-07-06): a native AppKit NSToolbar (mac/Sources/PhotoBlazeMac/ToolbarController.swift), the sibling of MenuBar.swift — every button fires a stable Action id via CoreModel.menuAction, and sync(MenuState, treeVisible) mirrors the live state (selected scale segment; Info/Folders/Slideshow on-state; Compare/Reveal/Delete enables). Chosen over a floating overlay strip because a titlebar toolbar costs zero extra image area in windowed mode, and Hide Toolbar (⌥⌘T) / Customize Toolbar… / fullscreen auto-hide are free native behaviors — resolving the chrome-less prime-directive tension. toolbarStyle = .unifiedCompact (the Preview-on-Tahoe look); the window title is split into filename + 'N of M' subtitle (applyWindowTitle). Default set: nav segmented, random, flexible space, scale segmented, rotate-left, inspector/tree/slideshow toggles. Allowed palette adds zoom, rotate-right, play, compare, copy, copy-path, reveal, delete, describe, open-file/folder, settings, fullscreen. SF Symbols (not FA) for system consistency. Compiles clean; produced a debug .app.

OPEN / ITERATE (needs on-device smoke — headless build here can't see it): (1) SwiftUI clobber — does it swap in its own window.toolbar on scene updates? reassertIfClobbered runs in assertWindowChrome (identity check, logged) to heal it; watch the trace. If it fights (flicker), consider dropping the .toolbarBackground modifier in ContentView and owning F-mode titlebar hiding purely via AppKit. (2) Look/legibility of the glass toolbar over bright/white photos (verify over a pure-white image — the known HDR all-white capture stress case). (3) Confirm the default button SET + order with the owner. (4) Toggle active-state rendering (pushOnPushOff recess + accent tint) — is it clear enough, or switch to a view-based recessed style? (5) Optional: transparent full-bleed variant (titlebarAppearsTransparent + fullSizeContentView in windowed mode) so the image runs edge-to-edge under the glass, the way the owner liked in the Preview Tahoe screenshot — a small follow-up once the button set is settled. (6) Windows/egui parity is still deferred to the egui presenter track (#54 subtask 5).

tasks.title: Auto-size the macOS Settings window to each tab's content
tasks.description: Owner gripe (2026-07-07): every new Settings control means hand-tuning a per-tab fixed frame height (SettingsView.swift TabView: General 615 / Appearance 615 / AI 645 / Shortcuts 640). Make it automatic — the window sizes to the current tab's natural content height. Prior art: vertical-only *user*-resizing was PUNTED after 5 failed attempts (see git history + the comment above the TabView, and the ns2-native-dialogs memory); this is the different goal of auto-fit-to-content, not user-resize.
tasks.details: Approach to try (needs ON-DEVICE iteration — SwiftUI window sizing can't be verified headlessly): the Settings scene already uses .windowResizability(.contentSize), so per-tab fixed frames are what pin the size. Options: (a) drop the fixed heights and let contentSize follow each Form's natural height — historically the Forms expanded to fill instead of reporting intrinsic height, which is likely why it failed; (b) measure each pane's content height (onGeometryChange on the Form's content, guard against feedback loops) and apply it as the frame height; (c) keep fixed frames but compute them from the content once at build. Watch for: the object_setClass/KVO segfault hazard on SwiftUI windows (never do that); jumpy resize when switching tabs; the window collapsing to min. Do it as a focused session with the owner watching, not a blind tack-on.

tasks.title: Linux port — winit/wgpu shell running on Linux (shipped & working)
tasks.description: The core is already cross-platform by construction: wgpu (Vulkan) + winit (Wayland/X11) render/window path, all pure-Rust decoders (jpeg/png/jxl/svg/raw/gif/webp/tiff). The OS-integration arms are ALREADY WRITTEN for Linux: clipboard (arboard #[cfg(all(unix, not(macos)))]), reveal (xdg-open), live-audio (no-op stub), menu (not(macos) muda path), HDR display query (default fallback). So the gaps are small. THE POINT of this task is not personal utility (owner wouldn't use it much) — it's DISTRIBUTION: the fast-culling niche (photos held resident in GPU memory, hold-to-fly) is genuinely underserved on Linux (feh/imv are CPU/basic, nomacs/Gwenview aren't fast, Loupe is a viewer not a culler), and the Linux crowd (r/rust, HN, r/linux) is the tastemaker audience most likely to try a Rust binary and amplify it. The definition of done for this task INCLUDES the companion blog post — a Linux port with no writeup is the 'vanishing on the cusp' pattern (built, never noticed). Ship the port AND the post together; that pays into both April Big Rocks (Build + Blog) in one motion. Owner lit up about this 2026-07-07.
tasks.details: GAPS (small, in bite order): (1) rfd file dialog — pulled default-features=false, so the O open dialog has no Linux backend; add features=["xdg-portal"] (or gtk3) to the cfg(all(unix, not(macos))) target block in pb-app/Cargo.toml. One line. Drag-drop file input works via winit regardless, so the app is usable even before this. (2) HEIC/AVIF: no WIC/ImageIO on Linux, so they silently drop; the libheif feature already exists and on Linux libheif is trivial (apt install libheif-dev) — none of the Windows vcpkg static-link pain. Build/ship with --features libheif. (3) set-as-default: Windows-only today; Linux wants a .desktop + xdg-mime story eventually, not needed for a working viewer. (4) Packaging: no installer; bare binary runs; AppImage/Flatpak later, optional. (5) Untested surface: Wayland vs X11 decorations, HiDPI/fractional scaling, GL fallback if a box has no Vulkan — shake-out, not architecture. HONEST CAVEAT: a third platform is a permanent support tax (CI, Wayland compositor fragmentation, bug reports forever); the code is nearly free, the support surface is not.

tasks.title: Anthropic (Claude) cloud describe backend — opt-in, extends #44's Describer seam
tasks.description: Owner ask 2026-07-08 (~2 AM). Add a first-class Anthropic/Claude vision backend to the AI-description feature as a THIRD backend behind the existing Describer seam (idle local RTX 5090 works today; this is a frontier-quality upgrade toggle, NOT a replacement — local stays the default). ⚠ CHARTER CHANGE, NOT A NEUTRAL ADD: task #44 is titled 'on-device / local models only', its design is governed by ADR-018 ('never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk'), and #44's own notes explicitly say '3rd-party server models (Anthropic/Google) ... not our path.' This task DELIBERATELY relaxes that: an EXPLICIT, opt-in, user-configured cloud backend is now allowed. That relaxation must be reconciled in ADR-018 + #44's privacy blurb FIRST (subtask 1) so shipping a cloud backend is a conscious documented decision, not silent drift — a Codex review will flag the contradiction otherwise. Note the seam already contemplates remote: the LocalEndpoint backend can point at any OpenAI-compatible URL and the settings already carry a 'custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL' privacy caption — so 'never cloud' has always meant 'never cloud silently/by default', and this extends that, it doesn't invent it. || WHERE IT PLUGS IN (all already exist, verified 2026-07-08): the Describer trait (prepared image + prompt -> text) in crates/pb-app-core/src/describe.rs; add an AnthropicEndpoint impl alongside LocalEndpoint. New DescribeBackend enum variant in settings.rs (currently Auto/AppleOnDevice/LocalEndpoint). Wire into describer_from_settings() at app_core_impl.rs (~line 4439). Prompt builder (prompt.rs), InfoMode::Describe panel, Ask flow, Copy, generation-cancel, RAM-only per-item cache are ALL backend-agnostic and reused unchanged — this really is just a new backend + secret handling + one settings option. || THE ONE REAL GOTCHA — Anthropic's /v1/messages is NOT OpenAI-shaped, so you CANNOT repoint LocalEndpoint: image is a base64 SOURCE block {"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/jpeg","data":"<b64>"}} (not OpenAI's image_url data-URI); headers are x-api-key + anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 (LocalEndpoint sends NO auth header today); response is content[0].text (not choices[0].message.content). Endpoint POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages. (An OpenAI-compat shim exists at api.anthropic.com/v1/chat/completions but it is a second-class beta and you'd have to add auth-header support to LocalEndpoint anyway — go native.) || MODEL: default claude-haiku-4-5 ($1/$5 per MTok, fast, vision-capable) — the honest sweet spot for library-scale captioning; offer claude-sonnet-5 for richer prose. NOT Opus (overkill + slow for alt-text). || SECRET HANDLING: new describe_api_key. Store in the OS keychain (keyring crate), NOT plaintext settings.toml; never log it. (Owner wrote secrt — credential hygiene is the standard here.) || NOT VIA GOLDFISH: owner floated routing through Goldfish/the Max subscription. Rejected — grep confirmed no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in ~/code/goldfish or ~/goldfish-tools; Goldfish runs on Claude Code / the Max subscription, whose OAuth auth is licensed for Claude Code / first-party apps, NOT for piping a separate app's API calls through it (ToS problem + brittle). This backend uses the user's OWN metered API key. If the real wish was 'Rachel can see my photos', that's a Goldfish capability (Claude Code already has vision), not a PhotoBlaze one — keep them separate. || v1 scope: on-disk stills, one-shot (streaming later), reuse the whole #44 pipeline. Distribution bonus: 'local-first image describer with an optional frontier backend' is a genuine blog-post bullet (April Big Rocks: Build + Blog).

tasks.title: Windows: folder tree (Shift+F) does not show for 7z archives
tasks.description: Owner-observed Windows gap (2026-07-09): opening a .7z archive with internal folders shows NO folder tree on Shift+F, while the same feature works for .zip. The tree derivation is SHARED and format-agnostic — crate::folder_tree::rows_from_names groups the deck's forward-slashed entry names (name(i)) into rows/counts/scope targets, and show_folder_tree_mode (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:1677) takes the archive branch whenever self.source.path(item).is_none() and walks full.name(i) over the unscoped source. ZipSource and SevenZSource are structurally identical to that code path: both return the full internal path from name() (via normalize_entry_name, pb-source/src/lib.rs), both return None from the default path() impl, and both return the archive file from container(). So a 7z with folders SHOULD produce the same tree a zip does. The divergence is therefore 7z-specific and the prime suspect is that sevenz-rust2's entry.name() on the block-decode/solid path (pb-source/src/lib.rs:697, normalize_entry_name(entry.name())) yields BARE FILE NAMES without the internal folder chain — folder_of() then returns "" for every entry, rows_from_names emits only the root row, and with a single row the tree looks like it 'isn't showing'. Verify empirically before assuming: dump (0..full.len()).map(|i| full.name(i)) for a folder-structured 7z and check the names actually contain '/'.
tasks.details: Where to look, in order: (1) Confirm the symptom's mechanism — is the archive branch even taken? Add a probe (debug build has a console) that logs, for the open 7z, source.path(displayed_item).is_none() and the first several full.name(i). If path() is unexpectedly Some, the disk branch runs and the wrong tree (or none) shows. If name(i) lacks '/', grouping collapses to the root. (2) If names are bare: the fix is in pb-source SevenZSource construction (both the streamed path ~line 485/586 and the parallel BlockDecoder path ~line 660-697) — ensure the stored SevenZEntry.name is the archive-relative PATH from sevenz-rust2, not a basename. sevenz-rust2's SevenZArchiveEntry exposes the full name; if for_each_entries hands back a stripped name, reconstruct it from the archive metadata. Keep normalize_entry_name (backslash->slash, ./ and leading / strip) so grouping matches the zip path. (3) Regression-test at the pb-source layer: a fixture .7z with nested folders (a/one.jpg, a/b/two.jpg, top.jpg) asserts src.name(i) returns the full slashed paths — mirror the existing zip name test (~line 1051). Then a folder_tree unit test already covers rows_from_names given correct names, so once names are right the tree renders. Note the counts/scope-target machinery, ScopedSource re-scoping, and Go prev/next sibling all key off the same name(i), so a name fix repairs archive navigation wholesale, not just the tree. Shared code, so the ZIP path must stay green.
tasks.testStrategy: Repro first: open a .7z containing nested folders on Windows, press Shift+F, confirm no/one-row tree; open the equivalent .zip and confirm the full tree — pinning the format divergence. Unit: pb-source fixture 7z asserts name(i) carries the internal folder chain (parity with the zip name test); folder_tree tests already assert rows_from_names output for good names. Manual after fix: Shift+F on the 7z shows the same folder hierarchy + counts as the zip, clicking a folder row re-scopes the deck, and Go prev/next steps across sibling archive folders. Confirm the zip tree is unregressed and nothing new is written to disk (privacy #2 — the tree derives from in-RAM names).

tasks.title: Smoother hold-to-pan / hold-to-zoom — gentler acceleration curve
tasks.description: Owner feel note (2026-07-09): holding the pan/zoom keys accelerates too aggressively and doesn't feel smooth — want a slower, gentler ramp with smoother motion. The hold-to-view loop is AppCore::apply_view_holds (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:5642), driven by the tuning constants in crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs: zoom e-folding rate ramps ZOOM_MIN_RATE 0.5 -> ZOOM_MAX_RATE 2.5 over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS 0.7 (exp() applied multiplicatively about center); pan speed ramps PAN_MIN_SPEED 450 -> PAN_MAX_SPEED 3200 px/s over PAN_RAMP_SECS 0.7. Both are already time-based (frame-rate independent, dt-clamped to 0.1s) so 'smoother' here means the FEEL of the ramp, not a timing bug. Two levers: (a) TUNING — lower the max rate/speed and/or lengthen the ramp so it starts and stays gentler (e.g. PAN_MAX ~1800-2400, ZOOM_MAX ~1.5-2.0, RAMP ~1.0-1.2s), a one-file constant change; (b) CURVE SHAPE — the ramp is currently LINEAR in t (min + (max-min)*(t/ramp)); an ease-in (smoothstep / t^2) keeps fine control longer at the start before building speed, which reads as 'smoother'. Optional stretch: a short release ease-out / inertia so motion doesn't stop dead on key-up. Shared-core feel change (helps macOS + Linux too), surfaced while testing on Windows; keep it a measured, owner-in-the-loop tuning pass, not a blind edit.

(2) Swap the linear ramp for an ease-in in apply_view_holds: factor the shared 'min + (max-min) * shape(t/ramp)' into a small pure helper (e.g. ease_in(u)=u*u or smoothstep) so zoom and pan share one curve and it's unit-testable (assert monotonic, ease_in(0)=0, ease_in(1)=1, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Keep the multiplicative exp() zoom-about-center and the pan clamp untouched. (3) Optional inertia: on key release, decay the last velocity over ~150-250ms instead of zeroing zoom_started/pan_started immediately — bigger change, own subtask, only if the owner still wants more polish after (1)+(2). Note the scroll-wheel/trackpad steps (WHEEL_ZOOM_STEP, PIXEL_ZOOM_STEP, WHEEL_PAN_STEP, PINCH_GAIN) are a SEPARATE input path (AppCore::scroll, not apply_view_holds) — the owner's note is about held-key motion, so leave the gesture constants unless they ask. Prime directive: this is off the photo hot path (only runs while a pan/zoom key is held), so feel is free to change; still no per-frame heap alloc. Consider whether any of these should become settings (nav ramp/start/max are already configurable) vs hard-coded; default to constants unless the owner wants a knob.
tasks.testStrategy: Primarily owner feel-test on device (Windows first, then confirm macOS/Linux unchanged-for-the-better): hold each pan direction and zoom in/out, confirm the start is gentle enough for fine framing and the top speed is comfortable, not lurchy. If the ramp is refactored into a pure ease helper, unit-test the curve (endpoints, monotonicity, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Regression: apply_view_holds still returns changed=true only while keys are held (loop keeps polling) and pan stays clamped to image bounds; keypress->photon nav timing is untouched (this path is nav-independent).

tasks.title: Cursor auto-hide option — hide the mouse pointer when idle / in speed mode (all platforms)
tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): let the mouse pointer hide, as an OPTION, on every platform where possible. Half the plumbing already exists but nothing actually hides today: contract::CursorKind::Hidden is defined (crates/pb-app-core/src/contract.rs:80) and its doc even claims 'the viewer hides the cursor in the chrome-free hot path and restores it on movement' — but (1) NOTHING in the core emits SetCursor(Hidden) (hover_cursor at app_core_impl.rs:2678-2686 only emits Grab/Grabbing/Pointer/Default), (2) the winit shell STUBS it: cursor_icon maps Hidden -> CursorIcon::Default (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs:3361, with the note 'Hidden is unused on the SetCursor path'), so Windows/Linux never hide, and (3) only the macOS shell honors it (CoreModel.swift:1897 NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true)) — and even that is dead code since the core never sends it. So this is: wire a core auto-hide POLICY, make the winit shell truly hide, confirm macOS, and expose it as a setting. 'Where possible': winit uses Window::set_cursor_visible(false) (works on Windows + X11; on Wayland cursor visibility is compositor-mediated and may be a soft no-op — accept graceful degradation there).
tasks.details: Design: (a) POLICY in core — after N seconds with no CursorMoved (and no panel/dialog/menu open, and pointer not over a clickable affordance), emit CoreEffect::SetCursor(CursorKind::Hidden); any real pointer movement restores the resolved cursor (Default/Grab/etc via the existing hover_cursor path). Drive the timeout off the existing tick-deadline machinery (next_deadline / self.now) — do NOT add a spin; the app already sleeps when idle, so schedule a wake at the hide deadline. A natural stronger default: in the borderless Fullscreen 'speed mode' (WindowMode::Fullscreen) hide sooner or immediately-on-idle, since that mode is the chrome-free hot path the contract doc references. (b) WINIT SHELL — replace the Hidden->Default stub: on SetCursor(Hidden) call window.set_cursor_visible(false); on any other kind restore visibility + set the icon. Track visibility so we don't thrash set_cursor_visible every event. Windows + X11 honor it; Wayland may ignore — that's the 'where possible' caveat, log/accept. (c) macOS — the core now actually emits Hidden; verify setHiddenUntilMouseMoves gives the desired feel, or switch to explicit NSCursor.hide()/unhide() (persistent hide with our own restore-on-move) if the until-mouse-moves auto-restore fights the policy. (d) SETTING — add a serde-default bool (e.g. settings.hide_cursor_when_idle, maybe an idle-seconds too) and surface a toggle in BOTH shells (egui Settings General/Appearance tab via a pb-ui toggle_with_label + the SwiftUI SettingsView), defaulting per owner (likely ON in fullscreen, or a simple global ON/OFF). Privacy #2: cursor state is ephemeral runtime state; the only persisted bit is the toggle in settings.toml — no viewing trace. Keep the policy pure/testable in pb-app-core (feed it 'now' + last-move time + mode + overlay state, assert it emits Hidden after the timeout and restores on move) so it isn't a shell-only behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: unit-test the idle policy in pb-app-core — given last-move time, now, window mode, and whether an overlay/affordance is active, assert it decides Hidden after the timeout and Restore on movement, and never hides while a dialog/menu/hover-affordance is up. Manual per platform: Windows (winit) — leave the pointer still over a photo, confirm it vanishes after the timeout and reappears on the first move; confirm it does NOT hide while hovering the Cancel-scan chip or with a panel/menu open; confirm it hides sooner/at-idle in fullscreen speed mode. macOS — same feel via the SwiftUI shell. Linux — X11 hides; note Wayland behavior. Settings: toggling the option OFF disables all hiding on every platform; the setting round-trips through settings.toml (and the SwiftUI FFI) and nothing else is persisted.

tasks.title: Live Photo motion: start playing before the whole .mov is decoded (streaming + decode-ahead)
tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): pressing P on a Live Photo takes several seconds to start because the motion .mov is decoded to a COMPLETE Animation before playback begins. decode_motion_job (crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs:245) calls pb_decode::decode_live_motion(path, edge) which decodes EVERY frame up front (ff_live.rs on Linux does a full FFmpeg decode of all ~44-90 frames; the Windows Media Foundation and macOS AVFoundation backends have their own latency). Two wins: (a) DECODE-AHEAD — after a short dwell (~1-2s) on a Live Photo still, eagerly kick the motion decode so P is instant when pressed (there is already an AnimWant eager-prep path via start_animation_decode + the `prepared` stash — confirm it covers Live Photos and tune the dwell); and (b) STREAM-PLAY — begin playback as soon as the first frame(s) are ready and keep decoding the rest in the background, instead of blocking on the full decode. This mirrors the app's core 'preview-first then refine' principle (CLAUDE.md) which currently is NOT applied to motion.
tasks.details: Today decode_live_motion returns a fully-populated Animation (all AnimFrames in RAM) and the pump only starts once it lands (poll_anim_decode). To stream: introduce a progressive decode seam — e.g. the decoder pushes frames over a channel (or into a shared growable frame buffer + a 'complete' flag) and the playback pump plays whatever is available, advancing as more arrive; if decode outpaces playback (it will — ~3s clip) it's seamless, and if it lags the pump holds the last ready frame. Keep it behind the same decode_live_motion seam so all three backends (Linux ff_live.rs, Windows mf_video.rs, macOS livephoto.rs) can adopt it; ff_live.rs is the easy first mover since we own the frame loop (decode_video_inner already builds frames Vec incrementally — hand them out as they're produced). Note the audio path (live_audio.rs / decode_motion_audio) already streams via pw-cat on Linux and native players elsewhere, so audio start is not the bottleneck — this is about the VIDEO frames. Decode-ahead (a): verify start_animation_decode(item, AnimWant::Prep) fires for Live-Photo items after the display dwell and stashes into `prepared` so P rebinds instantly; if motion isn't eagerly prepped today, wire it (respect the prefetch budget / don't decode motion for items being scrubbed past). Privacy #2 holds: motion frames stay RAM-only, dropped on revert/exit. Perf: never block the event loop; decode stays on the worker pool; the pump reads ready frames on the tick. Measure keypress→first-motion-frame before/after.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual: on Linux (WGPU_BACKEND=gl, --features livephoto) open a Live Photo, press P, confirm the first motion frame appears in well under the current several-second wait (ideally ~immediately once decode-ahead has run), and the rest plays smoothly without a stutter at the streaming boundary. Confirm decode-ahead: dwell ~2s on a Live Photo, then P — should be effectively instant. Confirm graceful behavior when navigating away mid-decode (no crash, frames freed). Cross-check Windows/macOS backends still work (even if they adopt streaming later). Pure-ish: if a streaming buffer type lands in pb-app-core, unit-test that the pump plays available frames and clamps to the last ready frame when decode lags.

tasks.title: Harden CI + toolchain against silent cross-platform drift (the gap that hid the Linux clippy debt)
tasks.description: The 2026-07-09 clippy cleanup (commit f71c0720) exposed two process gaps that let Linux-only debt accumulate invisibly. (1) rust-toolchain.toml floats `channel = "stable"`, so a newer stable silently promotes new future-incompat/clippy lints to -D warnings ERRORS: float_literal_f32_fallback (rust #154024) surfaced only in the AppImage build container on Rust 1.97 and never on the owner's 1.95 Mac. (2) CI never lints pb-app on Linux — ci.yml clippy's pb-app only on the Windows self-hosted runner (cfg(macos) stripped, Linux-dead code like the menu/HDR-finalize helpers never seen), Linux CI runs only `cargo test -p pb-core`, and the macOS runner builds only pb-mac-ffi + the host. Result: the Linux dead-code + lints were red for anyone building on Linux but green in CI. Close both so every platform's cfg-specific surface is linted somewhere and toolchain bumps are deliberate.
tasks.details: (a) Pin rust-toolchain.toml to an explicit version (channel = "1.9x.0") so lint churn becomes a reviewed bump instead of a surprise on whatever stable a fresh machine/container pulls; scripts/appimage.Dockerfile pins nothing either (installs `stable`) — align it to the SAME version so container builds match CI/dev, and document the manual-bump cadence. (b) Add a Linux clippy job to ci.yml: `cargo clippy -p pb-app -p pb-app-core -p pb-source -p pb-render -p pb-hud --features livephoto,pb-decode/libheif --all-targets -- -D warnings` on ubuntu (or the OrbStack appimage image), mirroring the Windows clippy coverage for the Linux cfg surface — pb-app is already Linux-clean as of f71c0720, so this just keeps it that way (and gates #70). (c) Optional: a macOS clippy step on the self-hosted mac runner for pb-mac-ffi + the engine crates with -D warnings, so the macOS cfg surface is gated too. High leverage, low effort.
